A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AutoToM, with matching core algorithms and five benchmark datasets despite changes to the title and organization. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original AutoToM benchmark accuracies, ablations, computational costs, and qualitative inference results in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark and embodied-assistance results, plus new comparisons of model outputs with previously published human judgments. These qualify independently of the reused human data.

M1.justification: The original model-discovery and Bayesian-inference loop is retained in Algorithm 1. V2 substantially extends the procedure to online goal inference: Algorithm 2 maintains, replenishes, reweights, and filters goal particles across timesteps. Appendix A2 also introduces a workflow for incorporating human feedback and recomputing an inference.

E1.justification: The five original question-answering benchmarks remain. V2 adds captioned cognitive-study scenarios covering online goal inference under full observability and desire/belief inference under partial observability. It also evaluates interactive household assistance on Online Watch-And-Help, extending coverage from answering questions to supporting sequential decisions.

E2.justification: V2 adds DeepSeek-R1, Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking, and o3-mini-high, while removing TimeToM, PercepToM, and the manually specified AutoToM comparison. BIP-ALM and LIMP now have comparisons across all five benchmarks. SymbolicToM gains Hi-ToM results, although Appendix A3.4 still says it was evaluated only on ToMi. Random Goal is added for embodied assistance.

E3.justification: The original benchmark sizes, ToMi preprocessing, Hi-ToM subset, and shared multimodal text inputs remain. New protocols include six goal-inference scenarios and seven food-truck scenarios, caption adaptation, probability or seven-point confidence responses, and Pearson correlations with human judgments. Embodied assistance uses 20 episodes across four task categories, a shared helping planner, and speedup relative to an unassisted agent.

E4.justification: V2 retains the five ablation variants and both original qualitative examples. It adds substantial analysis by question type, context length, agent count, and recursion level against reasoning models in Figure 4, extending beyond V1's narrower Hi-ToM order analysis. Figure 5 adds an inference trace, and Appendix A2 adds a case showing human feedback correcting erroneous extracted information.

E5.justification: V1 reports experimental point estimates without repeated-run counts, error bars, or significance tests. V2 introduces correlation significance reporting in Table 2 and standard-error bars for embodied-assistance speedup in Figure 7, with three runs per episode. These additions concern new evaluations; they do not establish increased repetition of the original benchmark experiments.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes AutoToM's MMToM-QA accuracy from 75.50 to 83.00 and its overall average from 80.93 to 82.43; BIP-ALM's MMToM-QA score changes from 76.70 to 56.17. MMToM-QA ablation and compute values also change. New results include human-judgment correlations of 0.93, 0.88, and 0.73, and assistance speedups of 27.7% for AutoToM versus 6.3% for Random Goal and 6.8% for GPT-4o. The PDFs do not explain the causes of all revised benchmark values.

T1.justification: The original Bayesian posterior formulation, entropy-based utility, recursive-state definitions, and model-space calculation are preserved. V2 adds a limited mathematical specification of sequential weighted-particle inference in Algorithm 2, including likelihood reweighting and normalization. It introduces no new theorem, proof, or theoretical guarantee.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes open-ended ToM and leading performance among general methods on each benchmark. V2 emphasizes scalable automated agent modeling and strongest overall performance against an expanded comparison set, including reasoning models. Its abstract, introduction, and conclusion add central claims about human-like confidence estimates and online inference supporting embodied assistance.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations connecting model confidence to human inference, uncertainty estimates to effective helping, and interpretability to correction through feedback. It removes the conclusion that automated discovery matches manually specified models. Its limitations add the lack of native multimodal inference but omit V1's specific warnings about irrelevant hypotheses, inaccurate likelihoods for similar hypotheses, and strict computational budgets.

D1.justification: V2 documents cognitive-scenario selection and captioning, household goal-generation rules, and online inference with 20 particles and a 10% filtering threshold. It adds reasoning-model identifiers, revises the belief-sampling prompt, and supplies an additional action-likelihood prompt. The original model-discovery hyperparameters and project/code destinations remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The three related-work strands and main positioning against handcrafted model-based inference remain. V2 adds citations concerning thought-tracing, DeepSeek-R1, SMC, planning with ToM, and altruistic helping, while dropping Wagner et al.'s Mind Your Theory and Ying et al.'s NIPE. These are bounded updates rather than a wholesale revision of the literature framing.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper, revises terminology toward agent modeling, and rewrites substantial portions of the abstract, introduction, related work, and experimental narrative. Experiments are organized into three studies, Algorithm 1 moves to the appendix, and appendix sections are reordered around implementation, feedback, and individual experiments. The separate ethics statement is removed and limitations are integrated with the conclusion.

P2.justification: V2 switches from two columns to one and substantially reorganizes displays. V1's Figures 3 and 4 become a combined Figure 3; Figure 2 gains cognitive-study and assistance panels. New displays include condition-wise comparisons, an inference trace, feedback interaction, human-model scatterplots, and assistance speedup. Table 1 changes grouping and structure, and new correlation and goal-definition tables are added.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation beyond V1's question-answering results: stronger reasoning-model comparisons, human-judgment analyses, and a controlled assistance evaluation test the psychological plausibility and practical usefulness of AutoToM's inferences. The appendices document these additions. Removing the manual-model control and several specific limitations weakens completeness, while unexplained numerical revisions and the SymbolicToM reporting inconsistency reduce transparency. Nevertheless, the new evaluations provide a substantial overall gain in support for the paper's central capabilities.
